fix: Return a borrow: `pub(super) fn selectable_text_value(&self, id: ElementId) -> Option<&str> { match self.elements.get(id.0)?.widget.kind() { WidgetKind::SelectableText { text, .. } | WidgetKind::Text { text, .. } => Some(text.as_str()), _ => None } }`. Read-only callers (static_selection_range at 1867, static_selection_text at 1922, selection_content_range at 1895-1901, which currently clones the whole text just for `.len()`) then borrow with no copy. Mutating methods that call `self.static_selections.insert`/`sync_static_selection` after reading the text (selectable_text_select, selectable_text_select_words_to, selectable_text_select_all, selectable_text_set_extent, selectable_text_move) add `.to_owned()` where the borrow of `self` would overlap, and selectable_text_editing_value returns `text.to_owned()` in its tuple.

Stop rebuilding the registrar list per call. `sync_static_selection` already computes `entries`; keep it on the per-area selection record (e.g. `StaticSelection` or a per-area `registrars: Vec<ElementId>` map updated in sync_static_selection and cleared when the area's registrations change) and have static_selection_range borrow it as `&[ElementId]`. Paint (painting/behavior/content.rs:34 and :60) calls this for every selectable element each frame while a selection exists, so the Vec from selectable_texts_in_area (line 1160) is a per-frame, per-element allocation. Interim: in selectable_texts_in_area line 1171 replace `.then_some(vec![area]).unwrap_or_default()` with `if matches!(...) { vec![area] } else { Vec::new() }` so the vec is not built on the non-selectable branch.

refresh_selection_states runs on every layout pass (layout.rs:117 and reconciliation.rs:1985). It collects a new Vec of areas (line 1356) and calls sync_static_selection on each, which builds entries, selection geometry rects, content range and selection text even when nothing changed, and calls mark_render_paint on every registered element (lines 1222-1226). Add a per-area dirty flag set when a selection changes, registrations change or text changes, and only sync flagged areas; iterate the boundary set with an index loop or reusable scratch buffer instead of collect::<Vec<_>>(). Also skip the paint marking when the selection geometry is unchanged. Confidence is medium because it depends on how often layout runs in idle frames.

with_text_field_display builds a fresh mask String on every paint and layout pass of an obscured field. Keep the mask on the field's render state (e.g. a `mask: String` in TextFieldRender) and rebuild it only when the byte length changes: `if mask.len() != value.text.len() { mask.clear(); mask.extend(std::iter::repeat_n('*', value.text.len())); }`, then pass `&mask` to `f`. Pass the mask storage into with_text_field_display (or make the helper a method on the render node) so the closure still receives a &str.

Return an iterator instead of a Vec: `pub(super) fn selection_rects<'a>(layout: &'a (dyn TextGeometry + 'a), selection: TextRange, scroll_x: f32, scroll_y: f32, top: f32) -> impl Iterator<Item = Rect> + 'a` and drop the trailing `.collect()` at line 1825. Callers then iterate directly: selection_geometry (line 1267) uses `selection_rects(...).map(|rect| transform.transform_rect_bbox(rect))` with `rects.extend(...)`, and paint (painting/behavior/content.rs:37 and :66) already loops with `for rect in`. This removes one Vec per selected element per paint.

`TextEditingController::text()` returns an owned String (incular-text/src/editing.rs:415), so this copies the whole field text on every pointer move during a drag just to take its length. Replace with `let text_len = controller.with_value(|value| value.text.len());`.

Borrow the text instead of cloning it per keyboard or pointer event: `field.controller.with_value(|value| line_boundary(&layout, &value.text, offset, affinity, forward, continues_at_wrap))` and return that Option. The same copy is made by `text_field_move_line_edge` (line 490-498) through this method, so it fixes both.

Use the std helper, which is a direct boundary search: `pub(super) fn valid_boundary(text: &str, offset: usize) -> usize { text.floor_char_boundary(offset) }`. The result is identical (largest char boundary <= offset, clamped to len), and it avoids iterating the characters. Called per element from static_selection_range on paint.

Each selected element allocates an intermediate String that is only pushed into the result. Build the result directly: `let mut out = String::new(); for element in entries { if let (Some(range), Some(text)) = (static_selection_range(tree, entries, selection, *element), tree.selectable_text_value(*element)) { out.push_str(&text[range.start..range.end]); } } out`. Pair with the borrowed selectable_text_value from the first finding.

`value()` clones the whole TextEditingValue (including the text) only to read the text length and emptiness. Use `let (len, is_empty) = field.controller.with_value(|value| (value.text.len(), value.text.is_empty()));`, then `let offset = if forward { len } else { 0 };` and pass `is_empty` in place of `value.text.is_empty()` at line 343.
